in_arabic.name: نَتارَات
in_arabic.long_meaning: الاسم نَتارَات، يعود أصلُه إلى اللُغة العَرَبيّة، ويتَأَويلُهُ إلى "الذات البَرِئَة" أو "الزَهراء المُبتَلىءة". في العَربيّة القَدِيمَة، كانَ هذا الأَسَمَ مُتَصَوَّراً لِلمَلكة أو الرِجالَة المُحَمَّدَة. في العَصور الوسطى، أُستَخدَم الأَسَم هذا في أَساطير المُلك القَدِيم. في العَصر الحَديث، أُستَخدَم الأَسَم نَتارَات كإسم لِلمُجَرَّدات في العَربيّة المُعَاصِرَة.

in_urdu.name: نَتارَات
in_urdu.long_meaning: نام نَتارَات کا تعلق عربی زبان سے ہے۔ اس کے معنی "بھرپور یا زرقارمغز" ہیں۔ نام نَتارَات کا استعمال اہل اسلام کی عورتوں کے لیے ہوتا ہے۔ اس نام کا استعمال قدیم عرب اور مسلم دنیا میں ہوتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: ऩतारात
in_hindi.long_meaning: नाम ऩतारात का अर्थ है 'भरपूर या ज़रुरतमंद'। इस नाम का उपयोग मुस्लिम समुदाय में होता है। इस नाम का संबंध अरबी भाषा से है।

in_pashto.name: نَتارَات
in_pashto.long_meaning: نَتارَات دې نوم د عربي ژبه څخه راځي، په عربي ژبه کې دا نوم ته د "بهرپوري يا زرقارمغز" معنا ورکول کېږي. دا نوم په افغانستان او پښتونخوا کې د مسلمانو عورتو لپاره کارول کېږي.

in_english.name: Nataarat
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nataarat has its roots in Arabic language and means 'the clear or the radiant one'. In Islamic tradition, the name Nataarat is associated with the qualities of purity and radiance. In Arabic etymology, the name Nataarat is derived from the root "n-t-r", which carries the meaning of clarity and brightness. In modern usage, the name Nataarat is used to convey the idea of a person who is pure, radiant, and full of light.

data.cultural_impact: In the Islamic culture, the term "Nataarat" is not a commonly used name for individuals or places. However, as a term, it represents the idea of something elegant, gentle, and beautiful, which aligns with the values of resilience, kindness, and refinement within the Islamic community. In various Islamic literature and poetry, the blooming of a nataarat flower is often used as a metaphor for personal growth, rise from adversity, or spiritual enlightenment.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, the nataarat flower holds deep symbolism within Islamic theology and culture. It serves as a reminder of the divine beauty and gentleness inherent in creation, which reflects the infinite wisdom, love, and mercy of God. As a blooming flower, Nataarat symbolizes the transformative power of faith and the potential for personal growth and spiritual evolution that comes with it. In various Islamic teachings, the nataarat flower also symbolizes the virtues of patience, perseverance, and resilience through adversity before reaching its beautiful and fragrant state. Particularly during the blessed month of Ramadan, the term nataarat has a spiritual resonance, reminding Muslims to cultivate their inner selves, nurture their faith, and blossom as individuals who radiate the beauty of submission to the Divine Will.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Nataarat is mentioned in the works of Ibn Khaldun (1332-1406) as a Berber tribe in the Maghreb. The name Nataarat carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun was a historian, philosopher, and sociologist. He is considered one of the founders of sociology and historiography. His works provide valuable insights into the history and culture of the Islamic world during the Middle Ages.
